newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Helix reports Gawler high-grade zones.
newsitem.headline: Helix reports Gawler high-grade zones.

text.p: Helix Resources NL said on Monday that recent drilling results from the closely-watched Gawler Craton region of South Australia indicated gold mineralisation over at least 1,000 metres and potentially mineable mineralisation restricted to about 500 metres.

The company said interpretation of the drilling at the Tunkillia Prospect indicated that the 500 metre zone contained a series of narrow high-grade zones ranging from 5.4 g/t to 25.5 g/t over drilled intervals of one to 14 metres.
"A single deep diamond drillhole appears to have intersected one of these zones at depth," it said.
Helix shares soared in late 1996 and early 1997 as investors and speculators focussed on the Gawler Craton as the next major gold region of Australia, reaching a record high of A$4.99.
The shares have slumped in recent months, however, as the company's drilling reports failed to justify the earlier speculative activity in the stock.
Helix shares were five cents higher at A$2.05 on Monday.

Major gold miner Acacia Resources Ltd bought a strategic 17 percent stake in Helix in February, paying about A$4.45 per share. Acacia said there was a good chance Helix had found a very large ore body in the Tunkillia Prospect.

Helix said that all drilling activity in the 1997 first quarter was targeted at further defining the mineralisation in Area 223 on the Tunkillia Prospect and at possible strike extensions and repetitions of the mineralisation.
It said the drilling consisted of 50 reverse circulation drillholes and three diamond drillholes.

"Results from this drilling defined a continuous zone of gold mineralisation over a strike of at least 1,000 metres although substantial, potentially mineable mineralisation appears at this stage to be restricted to the central 500 metres of strike," Helix said.

"Interpretation of RC and diamond drilling results has indicated that the 500 metre long main zone of mineralisation contains a series of narrow, high grade zones with assays ranging from 5.4 to 25.5 g/t gold over drilled intervals of one to 14 metres."
Helix also said that other drilling had shown anomalous gold in bedrock over at least 6.5 kilometres.
"Higher grade and broader zones of RAB (rotary air blast) gold anomalism are considered strong indicators of repetitions of the Area 223 mineralisation," the company said.
